## 1) Run AUB autopilot (module-level search + select-best)
```bash

  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --run --select-best
```
What to look for after it finishes:
- A report/artifacts indicating which module variants were evaluated and their scores.
- Whether it actually **promoted a new champion** (since `--select-best` can update the champion pointer/file depending on your tooling).
- Any failures/timeout notes that might explain why you have “no PASS candidates”.

If you want to be safe, snapshot the current champion file before running:
```bash
cp baseline/champion_v5_latest.json baseline/champion_v5_latest.json.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)
```

## 2) Run system autopilot (system-level candidates)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py \
  --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml --run
```
What to look for:
- Which system candidates were generated/evaluated.
- Whether any candidate clearly beats the champion on your primary metric(s), and whether regressions show up in the min/robustness metrics.

## 3) Generate the next-fix report (actionable remediation)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
This should produce a concrete “what to try next” plan (often based on recent failures, near-misses, or common error modes).
